extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners, communications staff, journalists, students and organizations issuing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for composing, formatting, distributing, and ethically vetting corporate or organizational press releases, including modern multimedia and distribution practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letterhead with company logo
rubrics_metrics.description: Include letterhead with company logo on the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard format component that signals official origin and credibility; usually placed at the top of the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: "FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE" or embargo notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark the release as immediate or include an embargo notice when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE' indicates the release can be published at once; embargo notices must clearly specify embargo terms and date/time to avoid confusion with journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline (city, state, date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a dateline including city, state, and date at the start of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dateline situates the news geographically and temporally — part of the standard press-release structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: A news-first headline that summarizes the most important news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headline should be written with a news emphasis (not marketing-speak) to attract journalist attention and convey the key point quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheadline (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: An optional subheadline that provides a secondary hook or clarifying point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to add context or a supporting fact when the headline alone is insufficient; optional and subordinate to the main headline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede paragraph (5 W's)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening paragraph that answers the five W's (who, what, where, when, why).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the most important information up front (inverted pyramid style); the lede should quickly give journalists the facts they need to decide on coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body (3-5 paragraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Main body of the release typically composed of 3–5 paragraphs providing supporting details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow inverted pyramid: most important details first, then supporting information; keep the body concise and focused to increase pick-up likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate (about company)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short boilerplate describing the company or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a succinct company description that journalists can reuse; keep factual and free of marketing hyperbole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide media contact details for follow-up (name, phone, email).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear contact information is essential for reporters to obtain quotes, clarifications, or additional materials; responsiveness is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: End marker ("###" or "-30-")
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an end marker such as "###" or "-30-" to signify the end of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traditional newsroom convention that signals no further copy; helps avoid accidental truncation or misunderstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverted pyramid structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize information in inverted pyramid order: most important facts first, then supporting details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit best-practice for news writing — improves readability and makes it easier for journalists to truncate or repurpose content.

rubrics_metrics.name: News-first headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the headline with a news-first orientation rather than promotional language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists favor headlines that present the news value immediately; avoid clickbait or purely marketing phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5 W's in opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the opening paragraph answers who, what, where, when and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential for journalistic utility — the lede should provide those basics so the story can be quickly assessed and covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive quote from spokesperson
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a quote from an organizational spokesperson that adds perspective or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes should be substantive (explain significance, provide insight), not mere platitudes; useful for journalists to add color and attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise and factual writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep prose concise and focused on verifiable facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid marketing hyperbole and jargon; concise factual language improves trustworthiness and increases the chance of media pick-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple distribution channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute the release across multiple channels (wire services, direct outreach, social media, company newsroom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wikipedia recommends wire services (PR Newswire, Business Wire, etc.), direct journalist outreach, social media amplification and posting to the company newsroom to maximize reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire service distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Use established wire services to reach broad media audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire services increase reach and deliver releases to newsrooms and databases; often used alongside targeted outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct journalist outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact journalists directly to pitch the story or provide additional materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalized outreach improves chances of coverage; tailor pitches to journalist beats and avoid mass, untargeted blasting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use social media to amplify the release and reach audiences directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement wire and direct outreach with social posts, multimedia assets, and social kits to engage audiences and journalists who monitor social platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company newsroom posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Post releases on the organization's own newsroom/web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as an authoritative repository and helps SEO; provides journalists and the public with a canonical version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in the press release must be truthful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics guidance emphasizes honesty; false or misleading assertions damage credibility and can have legal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiable sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Support claims with verifiable sources or data where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide citations, links, or references to underlying data to allow journalists to validate statements and reduce the perception of spin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of relationships / conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose relevant relationships, sponsorships, or conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about relationships prevents deceptive framing and maintains trust; the Wikipedia quality rubric explicitly lists disclosure of conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest framing (avoid deceptive framing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame information honestly and avoid deceptive or selective presentation of facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-patterns listed include selective fact disclosure and deceptive framing; honest framing helps prevent manipulation and reputational risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Be responsive to journalist follow-up questions and requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists expect timely responses for clarifications and interviews; Wikipedia lists responsiveness to follow-ups as a quality metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid enabling churnalism / clarity of source
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid producing releases that encourage verbatim republication or that masquerade as independent journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism notes press releases are often republished verbatim by understaffed newsrooms (churnalism) and can cause public information to be mistaken for journalism — clearly label releases as PR and provide useful, verifiable content rather than 'ready-to-publish' articles intended to substitute for reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid manipulative practices (astroturfing, strategic leaks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use deceptive tactics such as astroturfing, fake third-party releases, strategic leaks, or disguising PR as independent coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wikipedia highlights manipulation concerns — anti-patterns include astroturfing via fake third-party press releases, strategic leaks disguised as official releases, and other deceptive practices; avoid these to preserve credibility and ethical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider information-subsidy effects / equitable representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that press releases can disproportionately amplify wealthy organizations; consider balanced representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information-subsidy critique notes wealthy organizations can dominate the news cycle and marginalize smaller voices; practitioners should consider fairness and seek to avoid one-sided framing of public issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Include multimedia elements (images, video, audio, assets) to support the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern releases integrate multimedia to increase engagement and make it easier for journalists and social platforms to use the story; provide high-quality assets and captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media kits
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide social media kits (images, suggested copy, hashtags) to facilitate sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kits help amplify messaging and ensure consistency across channels; useful for both journalists and company channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Format content for readability and usability on mobile devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short paragraphs, clear headings, and mobile-friendly assets improve accessibility for journalists and audiences who access content on phones.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-summarization-friendly formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Format the release to be friendly to AI summarizers (clear lede, short paragraphs, explicit facts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As AI tools are increasingly used, structuring content for automatic summarization (clear key facts up front, consistent metadata) improves discoverability and correct machine-generated summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use real-time analytics to measure performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage real-time analytics to track reach and engagement of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern evolution encourages using analytics to refine distribution and measure impact (pick-up, traffic, social engagement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric summary (Wikipedia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate quality checklist including standard format components, truthful/verifiable claims, inverted pyramid, substantive quote, multiple distribution channels, disclosure of conflicts, responsiveness to follow-ups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wikipedia's 'Quality Rubric' consolidates many of the above items as a quick evaluation checklist for press-release quality and ethical standards.
